nodes.title: stambh/tally serves a level only when the mix-up's numbers are no single slip's and no other reading's: the packet lists six slips (a loose line missed / twice, a bundle skipped / twice, a bundle's line across missed / counted again) and seven readings (loose lines dropped / doubled, the line across as a sixth, the lines across alone, each group as one, each bundle as ten, the loose lines alone) with when each equals the mix-up. The law: no row with as many loose lines as bundles (6, 12, 18, 24); read 3, 4 or 6-9 bundles with a loose line; keep bundles in two rows or more, one of them two bundles, so the mix-up is at least three slips away and no choice of one slip or reading per row reaches it (read: two). sign=five only with no line across and >= 3 groups of five. Cost: fade 1 read is 16-19 (was 11-19) and keep 15-18 things (was 10-14). Reverse if: a pilot shows children slip in a way the list does not have, or the larger fade-1 scene tires class 4.

Tried (round 8, rounds 1-3): telling tally-four apart only from one-bundle slips (a bundle skipped or twice, one line off). Broke (evening judging, both judges): 2 bundles + 2 lines = 12; the mix-up gives 10, and so does counting the bundles right and dropping the loose lines, a reading the list did not have. Replaced by dc-r8-tally-slip-law (every slip and reading listed from the law, each asserted on every level).

stambh/tally: the count over each group plays, holds about a second and fades (gone about 3.5 s after the check; a tipped fifth line stands again); nothing stays over the tally while a try remains, since the 5s left over the bundles let her add up the key (law 2; evening ruling 2, replacing round-2 ruling 3's 'a 5 stays'). read's arrow shows after the first miss only; from the second miss her dot on the line and nothing else. Reverse if: children in a pilot miss the count (then a replay control, never a count that stays).

Central (every family, law 3): a mix-up from one pick among a few reaches the lesson exactly as an ordinary miss does until it repeats on another surface: no mid-level seam (was kind misconception with pick=1), no entry in the trail's mal, no chanceMis on the lesson's evidence rows (nameOnRepeat strips it from an unnamed row), and the trace records the moment as law_refused. The session still remembers it from the grade (afterLevelBody). On the repeat the row is named and the trail carries the mal-rule. kon/name find also stops reporting sign, vertex_ok and arms_ok (one tap tells nothing about the vertex). Reverse if: the lesson needs to know a one-pick miss happened (then a plain miss count, never the mix-up).

kon/name (both goals): a level is refused when reading the asked angle's letters off the screen like text puts the vertex in the middle: letters within one letter height (22 board px) are one row and within one letter width (16) one column, rows top-to-bottom or bottom-to-top and each row either way, columns likewise; by the points and by where their letters are drawn (labelPoints, which the view now draws from). find tries 1000 figures (was 160) because the rule refuses most; it still serves about 6 per request, keyed at the vertex about a third of the time and at a triangle corner otherwise. Reverse if: the picker's CPU p95 passes its 50 ms bar.

kon/name picker CPU after the read-like-text refusal (tests/_cpu-ms.mjs cpuNow, pickLevels x 60 requests, say + find, fades 1-3, seeds 700-729, this container): p50 15.3 ms, p95 19.0 ms, max 19.3 ms; bar 50 ms (round 2: p95 16-20 ms). With 1600 find tries it was p95 36 ms, so 1000 was kept.
